reviews.frank_statement: FRANK's recurrent loop-of-loops requires bounded executable control flow while all optional effects remain behind an external capability/effect gateway; recurrence decisions never become effect authority.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Static ClayCode effect declarations/transitive effect summaries can themselves serve as runtime execution authority, so a distinct fresh permit/capability identity is unnecessary.
reviews.falsifier: A production ClayCode compiler/runtime on the Ubuntu target safely executes the mandatory app/FRANK suite, including delayed recurrence and revoke/regrant/FFI escape tests, with no false allow/deny while collapsing effect summary and runtime authority into one mechanism.

independent_checks.finding: structured block/loop/if/call control is explicit validated execution semantics rather than model interpretation
call/control and memory-effect information are explicit compiler/IR properties and call-site information can refine function effects

independent_checks.source: Daan Leijen 2014 Koka row-polymorphic effect types
independent_checks.finding: potential side effects can be represented in function types and inferred compositionally

adversarial_checks.setup: effectful wrapper has correct transitive static effect closure; runtime permit is empty
same wrapper; runtime permit contains log.write
delete one actually inferred effect from caller declaration across 20,000 randomized graphs

reviews.reason: Independent language/compiler sources support explicit structured control and compositional potential-effect semantics, while the executable adversarial proxy rejects the stronger FRANK-derived assumption that static effect meaning may double as execution authority. The reusable result is therefore a generic ClayCode IR/type-effect contract with a separate fresh runtime permit boundary, not a FRANK-specific primitive.
